description: B11F's hash-on-mint uniform draw: the properties the preregistration stands on. That the key reads BOTH the seed and the mint (drop either and the draw stops being seeded, or stops depending on identity); that it takes the SMALLEST keys, so a larger N is a prefix-superset of a smaller one; that the size guards refuse rather than truncate or admit a boolean; that the selector's signature cannot silently grow an outcome input; and that build_subsample refuses a parent that is not a sealed fresh cohort, has no window, or was tampered, and never overwrites. Test (b), the pilot-isolation check, is not exercised by these mutants -- it guards a different tree (research/b11f/pilot) and is proven non-vacuous by its own planted-machinery tests in the baseline suite.

mutants.name: the key ignores the seed
mutants.note: Killed by the changed-seed test: a key that does not read the seed draws the same set for every seed.

mutants.name: the key ignores the mint
mutants.note: Every key becomes equal, the draw collapses onto the mint tie-break and stops depending on the seed -- the changed-seed test fails.

mutants.name: select the largest keys, not the smallest
mutants.note: Still nested as a set, but the tail is not a prefix of a larger tail; the prefix-nested assertion fails.

mutants.name: the over-population guard is removed, so N silently truncates
mutants.note: n beyond the population returns the whole population instead of refusing; making N a promise the data cannot keep.

mutants.name: the duplicate-mint guard is removed
mutants.note: A cohort weighting some curve twice would be drawn from without complaint.

mutants.name: the boolean-N guard is removed
mutants.old: if not isinstance(n, int) or isinstance(n, bool) or n < 1:
mutants.new: if not isinstance(n, int) or n < 1:
mutants.note: n=True is an int subclass; without the bool check a size of True quietly means one curve.

mutants.name: the N-below-one guard is weakened to N<0
mutants.old: if not isinstance(n, int) or isinstance(n, bool) or n < 1:
mutants.new: if not isinstance(n, int) or isinstance(n, bool) or n < 0:
mutants.note: n=0 slips through and returns an empty draw instead of refusing.

mutants.name: the selector grows an outcome input
mutants.note: The signature-shape test and the banned-activity-substring test both fire: 'signature_count' is a downstream quantity the selector may not name.

mutants.name: build no longer verifies the parent is a sealed fresh cohort
mutants.old: adapter.assert_fresh_cohort(source_path)  # refuses a non-cohort or an outcome-bearing one
mutants.new: source_path  # refuses a non-cohort or an outcome-bearing one
mutants.note: An outcome-claiming or hash-tampered parent would be read and re-sealed into a superficially valid subsample; the outcome-parent and tampered-parent tests fail.

mutants.name: the missing-window guard is removed
mutants.note: A parent with no provenance row unpacks None and raises the wrong error; the no-provenance test asserts the specific refusal.

mutants.name: the subsample artifact is no longer write-once
mutants.note: Rebuilding over an existing subsample would silently replace a population a downstream hash was taken against.

mutants.name: the recorded N is the population, not the draw
mutants.note: The audit metadata would misreport how many curves were drawn; the metadata test pins it to the requested N.

expected_survivors_note: None. Every mutant is in the draw's correctness or the artifact's refusals, each covered by an in-memory test over synthetic cohorts. The pilot-isolation property (test b) is deliberately not represented here: the sweep mutates the selector, whereas test (b) guards the pilot directory, and its non-vacuity is established in the baseline by test_the_check_flags_a_pilot_that_would_carry_machinery and test_the_check_flags_the_frozen_seed_literal rather than by a survivor here.
